This is open, and cannot be resolved with a finite computation.
Let $R_k(G)$ denote the minimal $m$ such that if the edges of $K_m$ are $k$-coloured then there is a monochromatic copy of $G$. Determine the value of\[R_k(C_{2n}).\]
#555: [Er81c]
graph theory | 
ramsey theory
A problem of Erdős and Graham. Erdős [Er81c] gives the bounds\[k^{1+\frac{1}{2n}}\ll R_k(C_{2n})\ll k^{1+\frac{1}{n-1}}.\]Chung and Graham [ChGr75] showed that\[R_k(C_4)>k^2-k+1\]when $k-1$ is a prime power and\[R_k(C_4)\leq k^2+k+1\]for all $k$.
This problem is #24 in Ramsey Theory in the graphs problem collection.

 Li and Lih proved that, for every fixed $(n\in{2,3,5}),$
$
R_k(C_{2n})=\Theta!\left(k^{n/(n-1)}\right)
\text{as }k\to\infty.
$
$
R_k(C_4)=\Theta(k^2)$
$
R_k(C_6)=\Theta(k^{3/2})$
$R_k(C_{10})=\Theta(k^{5/4}).
$
So, I think,
For (n=2,3,5), the order of magnitude is known and matches the Erdős--Graham upper-bound exponent.
Y. Li and K.-W. Lih, “Multi-color Ramsey numbers of even cycles,” European Journal of Combinatorics (2009)
